cards.text: About eight days after Jesus tells His disciples He must suffer, be killed and be raised to life (Luke 9:22), He takes three of them with Him: Peter, John and James. Out of the whole group, only THREE get the invite. Friend, the last time I got picked out of a group, I was in a clearance bin with a 25 cent sticker on my face.

cards.question: Jesus takes Peter, John and James up on a mountain. What does He go up there to do?

cards.text: Up on the mountain, as Jesus prays, the appearance of His face changes and His clothes become radiantly white. Friend, I scrub flour out of this apron every single day, and it has NEVER looked like that.

Then, SUDDENLY, two men are there talking with Jesus: Moses, who led Israel long ago, and Elijah, the prophet. Friend, if two people showed up in my bakery out of nowhere, I'd be face first in the chocolate chips.

cards.question: Moses and Elijah are talking with Jesus on the mountain. What do they talk about?

cards.text: Meanwhile, Peter and his companions are overcome by sleep, with Moses and Elijah RIGHT THERE. Friend, I'm the guy who falls asleep in the last ten minutes of every movie, so I'm not saying a word.

cards.question: True or false: by the time Peter and his companions wake up, Moses and Elijah are already gone.
When Peter and his companions wake up, they see Jesus' ___ and the two men standing with Him.

cards.text: As Moses and Elijah are leaving, Peter speaks up: “Master, it is good for us to be here.” I think Peter wants this moment to last, friend.

cards.question: Peter wants to put up three ___ on the mountain: one for Jesus, one for Moses and one for Elijah.
Right after Peter's idea about the shelters, Luke adds a short note about Peter. What does it say?

answers.text: He did not know what he was saying
He was speaking for all three of them
He had been planning it for days

cards.text: Peter isn't even done talking when a cloud appears and wraps all around them. I know that feeling, friend: the oven timer goes off every time I start a good story.

cards.question: True or false: the disciples are afraid as they enter the cloud.

cards.text: Then a voice comes from the cloud. Friend, when a voice speaks out of a cloud, even I stop talking.

cards.question: The voice from the cloud says Jesus is His ___, whom He has chosen.
After calling Jesus His chosen Son, the voice from the cloud gives the disciples a command: ___ to Him!

cards.text: After the voice has spoken, the disciples look around the mountain. I bet Peter isn't pitching any more shelters, friend.

cards.question: After the voice from the cloud has spoken, who is still there with the disciples?
True or false: in those days, the disciples tell everyone what they saw on the mountain.

findings.problem: The card identifies Moses as the one who led Israel and Elijah as a prophet. Those facts are not stated in Luke 9:30, and no references are supplied for them.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Luke 9:31 also says that Moses and Elijah appeared in glory, but no card tells that detail. Card 5 covers only their topic of conversation, leaving out a significant part of their appearance.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "He was speaking for all three of them" is not safely false. Peter has just used "us" and "Let us," expressly including the others in his statement and proposal, so a baker could reasonably argue for this answer.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The setup only says that a voice comes from the cloud. Nothing lets the baker reason out "Son" rather than "prophet" or "messenger," so this blank asks for an unseen word from the line rather than testing a meaning the baker can infer.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "Listen," "Pray" and "Bow" are all plausible responses to hearing that Jesus is the chosen Son. The setup does not distinguish among them, so the baker is guessing the exact verb rather than reasoning out the command's meaning.
